en.title: When We All Get to Heaven
en.author: Eliza E. Hewitt
stanzas:
[C]Sing the wondrous love of Jesus,
[G7]Sing His mercy and His [C]grace;
[C]In the mansions [F]bright and blessed
[C]He'll pre[G7]pare for us a [C]place.

While we walk the pilgrim pathway,
Clouds will overspread the sky;
But when trav'ling days are over,
Not a shadow, not a sigh.

Let us then be true and faithful,
Trusting, serving every day;
Just one glimpse of Him in glory
Will the toils of life repay.
en.chorus:
[C]When we all get to heaven,
What a day of re[D7]joicing that will [G7]be!
[C]When we all see [F]Jesus,
[C]We'll sing and [G7]shout the victo[C]ry!

notes: Text from Timeless Truths (Echoes from Heaven #192), which agrees word for word with the Cyber Hymnal's transcription of the first printing (Pentecostal Praises, Philadelphia 1898) except that the Cyber Hymnal prints 'traveling' and 'Heaven' capitalised; hymnary's representative text (Our Great Redeemer's Praise #616) agrees too, with 'ev'ry' and lower-case line openings. Tune HEAVEN (Emily D. Wilson, 1898), meter 8.7.8.7 with refrain. Key C: hymnary's instances run 49 C to 13 D-flat; TT prints C, already a guitar key. Chords derived from the Timeless Truths MusicXML score by reading the four-part chord on every beat. The score is an echo setting; the stanza's harmony is I with passing ii and IV (dropped), V7 alternating with I under 'Sing His mercy' (written V7), IV on 'bright and blessed' with a vii-dim7 of V on '-ed' dropped, and the cadence. Refrain: the 'What a day of rejoicing' bar passes through I6, iii and II7 (V of V) before V7 on 'be!'; the II7 is kept on 'rejoicing' because it is the bar's colour, the rest dropped. The E-major chords on the refrain's pickups are chromatic alto motion, not harmony.
